title: Register for sales tax where you have nexus
summary: Once revenue crosses state thresholds you owe sales tax where your customers are: connect billing to a tax platform, run the nexus study, register with each state’s department of revenue, turn on collection at checkout, and put the filings on autopilot.

parts.title: Choose a sales-tax platform
parts.guidance: Identify whether the company needs calculation, nexus assessment, registration, returns, remittance or several services. Compare platforms against its products, customer locations, billing systems and required jurisdictions, including exclusions and adviser involvement. Check integration and data-access needs before purchasing. A supported market in a platform does not determine whether the company must register or its product is taxable there.

parts.title: Connect billing data and run the nexus study
parts.guidance: Reconcile imported transactions to billing, including dates, locations, products, refunds and marketplace handling. Add physical business presence to the assessment. Check the platform’s flagged states against current state rules and measurement periods with the tax adviser. Preserve the data snapshot and assumptions; a detected threshold signal still needs a company-specific registration conclusion.

parts.title: Review the states where thresholds are crossed
parts.guidance: Examine each flagged state using actual sales, physical presence, product treatment and timing. Check the transactions counted under its rules and any marketplace effect. Resolve effective dates and possible prior-period exposure with the tax adviser before deciding to register. Resolve the flagged facts and record the basis for the registration decision.

parts.title: Register with each state’s department of revenue
parts.guidance: Prepare the registrations selected in the reviewed tax plan. Check the agency, account type, entity details, activity dates, signer and attachments against current instructions, then submit through the company’s authorized filing route. Track issued accounts and their filing schedules separately from pending cases. VAT or GST alternatives require their own local assessment and procedure.

options.title: Default — Streamlined Sales Tax registration
options.summary: Check which approved state registrations the Streamlined Sales Tax service supports. Review the selected states, entity, effective dates and resulting obligations before submitting through the authorized filing route. Track each state’s issued account and connect it to collection and return preparation. Use the appropriate separate registration process for states or taxes outside the service.

verify.how: Each state issues a sales-tax permit or account number — required before collecting tax there.

options.title: India - GST registration
options.summary: Assess the seller’s establishment, service, customers and transaction flow with the tax adviser to identify the appropriate Indian GST category. Check whether the non-resident online-services route actually applies. Use current official instructions for business and signatory details and the required filing authorization. After registration, establish the corresponding invoicing and return process from that Indian assessment.

references.title: GST portal non-resident online services registration

options.title: UK - one VAT registration (MTD)
options.summary: Assess establishment, taxable supplies, turnover and customer arrangements under current HMRC rules. Determine whether registration is required or elective and the effective date before preparing the application. Submit through the company’s authorized route, then use the issued registration to set up invoices, digital records and returns. Use the UK assessment to set the account’s tax treatment.
options.when: Indirect-tax registration in the United Kingdom

options.title: Germany - VAT ID + OSS
options.summary: Review establishment, products, customer status and transaction locations for German and EU VAT. Distinguish domestic registration or identification needs from an eligible One Stop Shop scheme and the transactions it covers. Confirm effective dates before authorized filings and configure invoices and returns accordingly. Keep obligations outside the selected scheme visible; OSS does not replace every national registration.

references.title: European Commission VAT One Stop Shop

options.title: France - TVA + OSS
options.summary: Assess French and EU VAT using the seller’s establishment, supplies, customer status and places of supply. Identify any appropriate One Stop Shop scheme alongside remaining national obligations. Resolve the registration plan before authorized submissions, then set invoicing, records and returns to that treatment. Separate scheme-covered transactions from those still requiring French or other national handling.

references.title: European Commission VAT One Stop Shop

parts.title: Enable tax collection on checkout and invoices
parts.guidance: Configure products, locations, exemptions and effective dates from the reviewed tax treatment. Test invoices, refunds and representative customer types before enabling the approved production changes. Reconcile early collected tax to expectations and confirm required registrations are in place. Decide how later product or customer-status changes reach the people maintaining tax settings.

parts.title: Schedule automated filings and remittance
parts.guidance: Use issued accounts and agency-assigned frequencies to schedule returns, including any required zero filings. Reconcile collected tax, refunds and credits before each return. Configure the company’s actual filing and remittance approvals and escalation for failed submissions or debits before enabling recurring actions. Keep acceptance and payment evidence with each return and revisit the schedule when registrations change.

metadata.supportReason: Tax platforms watch nexus thresholds, calculate at checkout, and file returns over their APIs; the state registration portals are manual form work and the exposure review is a judgment call.

geoNotes.summary: GST replaces the per-state sales-tax patchwork with one national regime — registration per state of operation on the GST portal; SaaS sold from abroad falls under the OIDAR rules.

Instead of per-state sales tax there is one national VAT registration — mandatory past £90k of taxable turnover (or immediately for many non-established sellers) — with returns filed digitally under Making Tax Digital.
One German VAT registration (plus a BZSt-issued VAT ID) covers the whole country; for EU-wide B2C digital sales a single OSS (One-Stop-Shop) return replaces per-country registrations.

One national TVA registration replaces the state-by-state patchwork — declared and paid through the espace professionnel — and for EU-wide B2C digital sales a single OSS (One-Stop-Shop) return covers every member state.

One national VAT registration (activated by the início de atividade declaration) replaces per-state registrations, and EU-wide B2C digital sales consolidate into a single One-Stop-Shop return instead of per-country filings.

Genuinely nexus-like: register for GST/HST once worldwide taxable supplies pass the $30,000 small-supplier threshold, then layer the separate provincial registrations — QST in Quebec, PST in BC, Saskatchewan and Manitoba — where your customers are.
